To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following problems are solved in the affirmative: (i) the induced-universal graph problem for n-vertex (ii) undirected, (iii) directed and (iv) bipartite graphs; and (v) the adjacency labeling scheme problem for n- vertex (vi) undirected, and (vii) directed graphs.

(i) the adjacency labeling scheme problem is solved for all classes of graphs; (ii) the induced-universal graph problem is solved for the class of all graphs, directed graphs and bipartite (and tournaments) graphs.
• Adjacency labeling schemes for undirected graphs, with optimal bit size, are achievable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of labeling vertices in a graph such that the adjacency of any pair of vertices is determined by the labels alone, without the need to know the structure of the graph.

the following question: Given an n-vertex graph, can we assign each vertex a label such that, given any two vertices and the labels of these two vertices, we can decide whether or not they are adjacent in the original graph?
the following problem: Given an undirected graph G=(V,E) with n vertices, is it possible to label the vertices in a way such that the labels are of length O(logn)?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for any graph G, there exists an induced-universal subgraph H of size O(|V(G)|2|E(G)|) such that any induced subgraph of G is isomorphic to an induced subgraph of H.
the best possible labeling schemes and induced-universal graphs for all these graph classes have been determined, with optimal results in most of the cases.
for every class of graphs, the best adjacency labeling scheme has a size of Θ(n/2), and the best induced-universal graph has size Θ(2n/3).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the adjacency labeling scheme of a graph can be used to construct an induced-universal subgraph of it with a similar number of vertices.
we have found a way to label vertices of any graph with a small number of bits so that given only the labels, we can efficiently answer any query about the graph.
the adjacency labeling scheme for a class of graphs is optimal if and only if there is an induced-universal family for that class of graphs with optimal cardinality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the fact that the problem we are considering seems very simple, it has a surprisingly rich combinatorial structure.

, in many cases, it is possible for a graph G to be represented by a set of labels of a size that is only slightly larger than the size of G, and that the labels can be computed in linear time, while preserving a number of properties of the graph, such as the adjacency relation.
the problem of labeling graphs is a useful tool in obtaining optimal constructions for induced-universal graphs, which is a fundamental concept in graph theory.
